verdict: Revenue rose 8% to $4.56B on strong pricing, and profit rose 8% to $592M as the Environmental Solutions business bounced back sharply.

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: 31.8% of revenue; profit before interest, tax and non-cash charges

kpis.label: Core price
kpis.note: Price rises added 5.3% to revenue while volumes fell 0.6%

segments.name: Collection
segments.note: Picking up waste and recycling from homes and businesses

segments.name: Transfer
segments.note: Transfer stations that consolidate loads, net of internal charges

segments.name: Landfill
segments.note: Disposal at Republic's own landfills, net of internal charges

segments.name: Environmental Solutions
segments.note: Hazardous and special waste treatment and field services, net of internal charges

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Recycling processing and commodity sales ($122M) plus other small lines ($111M)

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion and amortization
opex.note: Non-cash charge spreading the cost of trucks, landfills and bought intangibles over their lives

opex.name: Accretion
opex.note: Yearly growth in the future cost of closing and monitoring landfills

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Costs of a systems redesign project

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$202M is $157M of interest expense plus a $48M loss from equity-method investments, partly offset by $3M of interest income. The -$1M equity line is the profit share belonging to a noncontrolling partner, so net income is the amount attributable to Republic shareholders.

takeaways.title: Pricing did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Revenue reached $4.56B. Core price increases added 5.3% and acquisitions 1.3%, while volumes slightly declined.

takeaways.title: Environmental Solutions rebounded
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $529M from $433M and its adjusted profit margin improved to 25.4% from 21.0% a year ago.

takeaways.title: Guidance up, new buyback approved
takeaways.text: Republic raised its full-year revenue and profit guidance and the board approved a new $5B share-buyback plan running 2027–2029.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $4M in the quarter ($10M year to date) for designing a new accounts-receivable system.
